newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's UDF nominates Ivan Kostov as new PM.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's UDF nominates Ivan Kostov as new PM.

text.p: Bulgaria's Union of Democratic Forces on Thursday nominated party leader Ivan Kostov as prime minister following its victory in Saturday's parliamentary elections, national radio said.
The nomination must be approved by the new parliament which is expected to convene on May 5.

The UDF and its coalition allies won 52 percent of the vote and 137 seats in the 240-seat parliament, compared to 22 percent and 58 seats for the former ruling Socialists. Three smaller parties will also be represented.

The radio said the former chairman of the UDF parliamentary group, Yordan Sokolov, would be nominated for parliamentary speaker, and the group's former deputy chairwoman, Ekaterina Mikhailova, would lead the party in parliament.
Kostov was a central figure in month-long daily protests which toppled the Socialists in February and forced the holding of elections nearly two years early.
All five parties to be represented in parliament have given their broad support to the UDF's programme for leading the country out of crisis.

The UDF's stated priorities are carrying out reforms agreed with the International Monetary Fund, fighting organised crime and corruption, opening secret police files on public figures, and bringing Bulgaria into the European Union and NATO.
The party leadership said it expected laws for implementation of a currency board fixed exchange rate regime to be passed by the end of May.
Kostov, a former finance minister, has invited an IMF mission to visit from May 6 to finalise the 1997 budget and amendments to the banking laws.
He said on Wednesday that Bulgaria's macroeconomic performance had improved in the past month and that the 1997 budget frame agreed with the interim cabinet in March would need to be adjusted.
First signs of stabilisation were seen after the two-month rule of the caretaker cabinet appointed by President Petar Stoyanov and led by Sofia's popular UDF mayor, Stefan Sofianski.
Monthly inflation has slowed to 4.5 percent in April from 12 percent in March and 243 percent in February and the lev currency has stabilised.
